title: The full Claude Platform, available on Google Cloud
summary: Claude Models on Google Cloud in Anthropic-managed mode is now generally available, giving Google Cloud customers the full Claude Platform feature set, billed on a single Google Cloud invoice against existing commitments with Google Cloud IAM credentials. Managed Agents, the MCP connector, and some other features are in beta, while Fast Mode on Claude Opus 5.5 is GA at $8/$40 per million input/output tokens. Customers can choose Anthropic-managed (Anthropic is the data processor) or Google-managed (Google is the processor, with regional residency and Model Armor/Agent Engine) deployment.

title: Building agents: When to fold subagents into your main agent loop
summary: This guidance recommends replacing multi-subagent setups with a single main agent loop that uses one model, one context window, and skills, with tools loaded on demand. Anthropic claims this often beats one-prompt and subagent designs on quality and is usually cheaper and faster, with one customer seeing roughly 2x faster runtime. Teams should build a small end-to-end eval, fold in one subagent at a time, and keep subagents only for context bloat, parallelism, or conflicting instructions, with a migration kit now available.

title: Redesigning source control at Anthropic
summary: Anthropic's engineering team describes Scion, an in-house source control system that replaces git for its monorepo, plus the Antique code review tool, migrated in about five months. Reported results include roughly 200x less CPU and memory than prior git mirrors, checkouts dropping from minutes to seconds, and daily merged changes rising from about 2,500 to 30,000+. The approach is shared so git platforms can adopt parts of it.

title: How the Claude Code team does code review
summary: The Claude Code team describes its review process now that Claude writes about 90% of the codebase, with most review automated and humans focused on risky decisions. From June to September, merged PRs more than doubled while the revert share fell over 40%, and review rounds are capped at three with only new diffs re-reviewed (mean reviews to pass fell from 2.08 to 1.32). The post also covers agent-verified findings, risk-scaled human approvals, and an adoption checklist.

title: Claude Cowork and chat come together for Enterprise
summary: Chat and Cowork are now unified into one Claude experience across web, desktop, and mobile, and this is generally available for Enterprise plans. Users don't pick a mode up front: a chat continues as agentic work in the cloud when a task needs code or files, and tasks keep running after the laptop closes and can resume across devices. Admins get role-based access, a new Efficient mode limited to Sonnet and Haiku, and spend controls per org, group, and member, with SSO and Compliance API controls carrying over.

title: Claude Security now scans continuously and tracks fixes
summary: Claude Security is in public beta for Enterprise, powered by Claude models including Claude Mythos, and connects to repos via a GitHub app or tokens for a baseline scan followed by risk-based rescans. It marks findings fixed when code lands and reopens them automatically if the issue reappears, with a per-project knowledge base, an editable threat model, and severity and attacker-reachability details. A new API, MCP connector, webhooks, and role-based access controls round out the release.
